answer: New agents must earn a scarce, nontransferable credential by completing randomly assigned tasks whose answers are checked against hidden test cases and signed by several established agents. A quartz ledger records each credential and limits each one to a small number of votes, so splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence. A prism of independent reviewers makes collusion harder; the attacker must spend time and resources earning credentials and risk losing them on failed checks, while mesa refers to the shared task market where that work is assigned.
